subject: Discovery recap — Finly: p95 latency, streaming UX & concurrency requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Harris <tom.harris@finly.com>, Priya Shah <priya@finly.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap — Finly: p95 latency, streaming UX & concurrency requirements

Thanks for the call today — good to meet the Finly team. Quick recap from our side and a proposal for next steps so we can align on a scoped PoC. Please confirm or correct anything I missed.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- End users seeing stutters and delayed partial responses in the streaming chat UI (bad UX for 8–10s responses).
- Backend spikes causing p95 response times that exceed your SLA during batch processing windows.
- Cost unpredictability when traffic spikes (30–40% variance month-over-month).

Current stack you described:
- Frontend: React SPA with streaming websocket connections to a backend proxy.
- Backend: Internal inference service on AWS (NVIDIA instances) that currently routes to several model variants; some calls hit external hosted APIs.
- Observability: Prometheus + Grafana for infra; limited token-level tracing for inference calls.

Success criteria for PoC (proposed):
1) p95 generation latency for short conversational queries (<= 600ms) for 90% of regular traffic.
2) Consistent streaming UX: first partial chunk delivered within 150ms and consistent subsequent chunk cadence with no >800ms gaps.
3) Support sustained concurrency of 600 concurrent live sessions with bounded tail latency under expected traffic profile.
4) Demonstrable unit-cost reduction (tokens/second cost) or predictable cost per 10k requests.

Immediate next steps:
- Redwood to provide a short design for a PoC (runtime config, estimated infra, expected throughput) — attach by EOD Monday.
- Finly to share a representative traffic trace (example logs/latency distribution) and a short list of 3–5 sample prompts for QA.
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with Aditya and Dylan next week to go over KV caching, batching, and streaming chunk behavior.

I attached a one-page recap and a rough estimate workbook for initial sizing. Happy to hop on a quick sync to align.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 17:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — Finly: p95 latency, streaming UX & concurrency requirements

Thanks Marissa — this is a great recap and captures the main items. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Our current p95 across the board is ~1.8s for short (~200 token) responses; p50 is ~350ms. The spikes come during our batch reconciliation window at 3am (customer batch writes that fan out inference jobs).
- Streaming UX: customers expect near real-time typing experience. If the first token takes >200ms they perceive the session as laggy. We see many sessions where the first partial arrives ~600–900ms.
- Concurrency: baseline active sessions are ~120, peak can exceed 700 for short periods (promo-driven). For PoC we should target sustaining 600 concurrent streaming sessions with graceful degradation past that.

We'll share a 48-hour trace (anonymized) and 5 sample prompts by Monday. 

One question: for streaming, can Redwood guarantee initial partials under 200ms on a PoC infra? If not guaranteed, what mitigations (prefetch, warm pools, KV caching) do you recommend?

I'll be available for the tech deep-dive next Wed afternoon (PDT).

Best,
Tom Harris
Head of Product — Finly
tom.harris@finly.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 26 Jun 2027 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — Finly: p95 latency, streaming UX & concurrency requirements

+1 on the summary. Technical notes for the deep-dive and what we'll prep for the PoC: 

- Initial partials: we can usually deliver first chunk <=150ms if requests hit a warm runtime + KV cache for prompt prefixes. For short prompts the overhead is kernel launch + network + scheduling — we'll quantify in the design doc.
- Autoscaling + warm pools: propose a mixed strategy (pre-warmed containers for steady baseline + burstable spot-like pools for promotions). We'll include projected cost delta in the workbook.
- Batching strategy: continuous batching for short/streaming queries (small window sizes) + larger batch jobs for offline reconciliation. We can route reconciliation traffic to cheaper model variants during batch windows to avoid tail impact.
- Observability: we'll propose token-level tracing hooks and a short dashboard (p50/p95/p99 per route, chunk cadence heatmap).

Deliverables for Monday EOD (Marissa):
1) PoC design doc (runtime topology, warm-pool sizing, expected p95 numbers under tested concurrency).
2) Sizing workbook (the attached XLSX is a starting point; I'll fill the perf columns).
3) Agenda for Wed tech deep-dive.

I'll also bring a short demo showing streamed partials from our runtime (to illustrate chunk cadence and gap behavior).

- Aditya
